meta.title: Quenderin — Local AI for Mac and iPhone
meta.description: Quenderin is an open-source app for running language models on your device. Chat works offline after downloading a model. Available for Mac and iPhone.
lang.label: Language
hero.title: Language models on your own device.
hero.lede: Quenderin is a free, open-source app for Mac and iPhone. Download a language model to write, ask questions, and work with text locally. Once the model is installed, chat works without an internet connection.
agent.title: Computer tools through the macOS CLI
agent.body: The source CLI can use a local model to organize files, interact with Mac apps, and run Apple Shortcuts. These tools have permissions and controls for reviewing actions:
agent.p1: Action approval. The CLI asks before changes by default. App control requires approval even when auto-approve is enabled.
agent.p2: Task history. Review the local log with quenderin history. Use quenderin undo to reverse supported file operations.
agent.p3: Preview. Use --dry-run to inspect proposed actions before running them.
agent.p4: Local processing. The model runs on your Mac. Apps and Shortcuts it interacts with may use their own network connections.

problem.title: Local chat, including when you’re offline.
problem.body: Quenderin runs the model on your device and stores your conversations there. It can help with drafts, explanations, and code. Response quality and speed depend on the model and your hardware; answers can be incorrect. See the measurements and limitations.
how.title: Choose a model, download it, and start a chat.
how.s1b: Quenderin checks your memory and processor to recommend a model for your device.
how.s2b: Choose a model and download it over an internet connection. File sizes are listed before you download.
how.s3b: After the model is installed, you can start and continue conversations without internet access.
feat.title: What the app includes
feat.offline.b: Once your model is installed, chat works without an internet connection. Model discovery and downloads need a connection.
feat.offline.m: The installed model runs on your device through llama.cpp. Downloads, model search, and release-list updates use the internet; they do not send your chats or attached files.
feat.free.b: The app has no subscription or per-message charge.
feat.free.m: Replies are generated on your hardware, without a paid inference service. The app’s source code is available under the MIT license.
feat.agent.b: The apps include local tools. Broader Mac app control is available through the source CLI. Safety checks restrict sensitive actions involving:
feat.agent.m: Tool availability and approval controls differ between the apps and the source CLI. The CLI provides a task log, action previews, and undo for supported file operations. Review actions before allowing them.
feat.priv.b: Chat history stays on your device. No account is required.
feat.priv.m: Quenderin does not send conversations to an inference service or collect analytics and telemetry. Model downloads, optional search, and release information use network requests.
feat.hw.b: Memory estimates help you choose a model for your device.
feat.hw.m: The model library shows whether a model fits, is tight on memory, or is too large. These are estimates; available memory and model settings affect performance.
feat.os.b: The source code is available under the MIT license.
feat.os.m: The repository contains the app code, model integration, and tool safety checks, along with build instructions.
feat.resume.b: Interrupted model downloads can be resumed.
feat.resume.m: Quenderin supports resuming interrupted downloads and checks model files before loading them. Background download behavior depends on the platform.

faq.title: Common questions
faq.intro: Details about cost, privacy, supported devices, and installation.
faq.a1: Quenderin is free to use, with no subscription or per-message charge. Models run on your own hardware. The app’s source code is MIT licensed.
faq.a2: Your chats and files stay on your device. Model downloads, optional catalog search, and release metadata use network requests; inference works offline. There are no analytics, accounts, or telemetry.
faq.q3: What devices does it run on?
faq.a3: Quenderin is free on the App Store for Mac and iPhone. Windows and Linux previews are available from GitHub. The native Android app is in closed beta on Google Play.
faq.q4: Do I need a powerful phone?
faq.a4: Model requirements vary. Quenderin estimates which models fit your device’s memory. Smaller models use less memory, but their answers may be less capable.
faq.a5: The Mac and iPhone apps are on the App Store. The download page also links to Windows and Linux previews and the Android closed beta.

foot.tag: An open-source app for local language models.
foot.note: No cookies, analytics, or trackers—nothing loads from a third party.
hw.lede: Quenderin turns your phone or laptop into a self-contained AI. There's no server doing the thinking for you — the model itself lives on your device. Setup is three steps, and it only happens once.
hw.s1b: On first launch, Quenderin reads what your device actually has — total and free RAM, the chip, and whether there's a usable GPU. It uses that to recommend the largest model your device can run well, not just the largest one that fits. If nothing fits comfortably, it tells you plainly instead of stalling.
hw.s2b: Pick the recommendation or choose your own — anywhere from a 0.4 GB ultra-light build to a 9 GB flagship. The download runs over Wi-Fi and resumes in the background if you switch apps or lose signal, so a big model finishing overnight is no problem. Every download is integrity-checked before it's ever loaded.
hw.s3b: From then on, everything runs locally. Before you leave the grid, a clear check confirms the model is present and ready — a green "ready to go offline". After that, airplane mode, a tunnel, or three days on a trail make no difference.
hw.od.b: Most assistants are a thin app in front of someone else's data center. Quenderin is the opposite: the weights, the inference, and your conversation history all stay on the hardware in your hand.
hw.od.c1: No prompt or response is ever sent to a server
hw.od.c2: No account, no sign-in, no API keys to manage
hw.od.c3: No analytics or telemetry — there's nothing phoning home to disable
hw.od.c4: Conversations are stored locally and are yours to delete
hw.od.c5: The one and only network call is the initial model download
hw.rs.t: It picks a model that actually runs.
hw.rs.b1: Bigger isn't always better on a phone. Quenderin matches the model to your device's memory headroom, leaving room for the operating system so things stay responsive — and it warns you before a model that would swap, stutter, or fail to load.
hw.rs.b2: The result: a capable assistant that feels instant, instead of a flagship model that crawls. You can always override the recommendation and choose your own trade-off.
ft.lede: Quenderin isn't a stripped-down toy because it runs locally — it's a capable assistant that happens to need nobody's servers. Here's what that buys you.
ft.offline.b: Download a model once and use it without internet. Browsing new models and downloading files uses a connection; your chats stay on your device.
ft.free.b: No subscriptions, no per-token billing. Inference runs on hardware you already own.
ft.agent.b: Quenderin includes a tool-using agent that can carry out small tasks — but it ships with a hard safety blocklist it can never override on its own. It will not autonomously pay, delete, transfer money, or touch credentials. Sensitive actions are surfaced for you to confirm, never taken silently.
ft.priv.b: No accounts, no analytics, no telemetry. Your conversations stay on your device — and because it's open source, that's verifiable, not a promise.
ft.hw.b: It picks a model that fits your memory and chip — and warns you before one that doesn't, so it never stutters or fails to load.
ft.os.b: MIT licensed. Read every line, audit every privacy claim, and build it yourself from source.
ft.resume.b: Models keep downloading in the background and resume after an interruption — switch apps the night before a trip and it's still ready by morning.
ft.cta.b: Every feature above works with any model you choose — from a Raspberry Pi build to an M-series flagship.
md.intro: Quenderin runs on llama.cpp, so it runs any GGUF model — Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Gemma, Phi, and thousands more from Hugging Face. Below is the curated shortlist it recommends from, sized for everything from a Raspberry Pi to an M-series Mac.
md.foot: + thousands more from Hugging Face — any GGUF works.
md.rec.b1: Choosing a model is optional. Quenderin detects your device's memory and chip and automatically selects the best fit — leaving headroom for the operating system so the app stays responsive. It steers you away from a model that would swap to disk or fail to load.
md.rec.b2: Prefer to drive? Override the recommendation and load any GGUF you like, including ones you've downloaded yourself.
md.q.b1: The catalog defaults to Q4_K_M quantization — a 4-bit format that cuts a model's size to roughly a quarter of full precision while keeping almost all of its quality. That's what makes a 7-billion-parameter model fit, and run, on a phone.
md.q.b2: Larger quants (more quality, more memory) and smaller ones (lighter, faster) are available for any model you bring.
md.cta.b: It's open source and runs from GitHub today. Star the repo to follow along.
fq.a.models: Any GGUF model on llama.cpp—Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Gemma, Phi, and thousands more from Hugging Face. See the model catalog for the curated shortlist it recommends from.
fq.q.agent: Can it actually do things, or just chat?
fq.a.agent: Yes — a lot. On a Mac it can organize files, drive apps, and run your Apple Shortcuts (the launch post has the details). It's a governed agent: it asks before every change, keeps a local log you can review, and can undo a whole task. A hard safety blocklist it can't override means it will never autonomously pay, delete, transfer money, or touch credentials.
fq.q.agentsafe: Can the agent mess up my computer?
fq.a.agentsafe: By design, it's hard to. Nothing that changes anything runs without your explicit yes for that step; file tasks are limited to a folder you grant, and never overwrite or truly delete (things move to a visible Trash you can restore from). You can stop it instantly with Ctrl-C, and quenderin undo reverses the last task — even in a new session, an hour later. Want to look before you leap? --dry-run shows exactly what it would do while changing nothing.
fq.q.size: How big is a model download?
fq.a.size: Your choice—from about 0.4 GB for the ultra-light build to 9 GB for the flagship. It downloads once over Wi-Fi and resumes in the background if interrupted.

catalog.intro: Choose a model for the work you do and the device you have. Explore new releases below, or start with a curated choice from Quenderin’s shared app catalog.
catalog.note: RAM figures are estimates, not minimum device memory. The app checks your chip, free memory and storage. *Paged MoE needs a fast SSD and a much larger download; installed app versions may offer different built-in choices.
catalog.liveintro: Recent GGUF releases from recognized model authors, refreshed hourly. Newer is not always better for your device: check the model card and try it through Models search in the app.
catalog.discoverycaveat: These are newly discovered files, not tested app recommendations. Download size is not RAM usage; engine support and speed vary by device. Multimodal model cards do not imply image or audio support in Quenderin.
catalog.explore: Explore the full catalog and device guide →
catalog.empty: No recent release in this download range. Try a larger range or a curated model below.
catalog.fitintro: A starting point for a Mac or Linux computer. iPhones have a smaller per-app memory budget: use the app’s device check for your phone.
catalog.ctabody: Get Quenderin on your Mac or iPhone. Open Models to find a choice that fits, then download it once.
catalog.quantbody: Quantization compresses the weights. Q4_K_M is a common balance; smaller quants save space at a quality cost. The right format also depends on the model architecture and your inference engine.
